CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old female who presents with right leg pain sustained during a bowling injury. She reports that while bowling, she swung her bowling ball forward and inadvertently struck the top part of her right leg with the ball, after which she fell. She denies significant swelling but reports some bruising on the back aspect of the leg. She has been able to walk only with great difficulty and pain. She reports the pain is very sore with ambulation and would avoid stairs at all costs. She has been managing pain at home with alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies swelling of the leg. Reports some bruising on the posterior aspect. Denies pain with passive flexion or extension of the lower leg.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Atopic eczema
2. Diverticulosis with history of diverticulitis, status post colectomy

MEDICATIONS
1. Fluocinonide (topical) - used as needed for eczema
2. Ibuprofen - as needed for pain
3. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) - as needed for pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient engages in recreational bowling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to palpation over the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with passive flexion or extension of the lower leg. No significant swelling appreciated.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: Normal. No evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right leg contusion. Start mobic 15 mg once daily. Ice for pain management. Anticipate improvement within one week. Patient to return if symptoms do not improve.
